newsitem.title: GERMANY: Toepfer details EU 1997 oilseed estimates.
newsitem.headline: Toepfer details EU 1997 oilseed estimates.

text.p: German grain trader Alfred C Toepfer on Friday forecast the European Union oilseed area in 1997 at 5.5 million hectares, up three percent from 1996.
Toepfer in its monthly newsletter also said the rapeseed crop might be 7.7 million tonnes after 7.2 million tonnes in 1996 while the sunseed crop was expected unchanged at four million tonnes.
Toepfer's area estimate was broadly in line with figures announced last Friday by the European oilseed lobby ANGO.
The rapeseed area was put at 2.7 million ha, up two percent, and the sunseed area at 2.4 million ha, also up two percent.

The non-food area for industrial oilseed was put at 400,000 ha, down from 650,000 ha, which might imply an overshoot of the 4.93 million ha subsidised food area limit set under a bilateral agreement with the U.S., Toepfer said.
This was arranged under the 1992 Blair House agreement, which put the area limit at 5.482 million ha, less 10 percent compulsory set-aside.
Toepfer added that the area sown to pulses had been expanded by an overall three percent.
Feed peas were planted on 890,000 ha (up from 850,000 last year) while the feed beans area was down five percent at 217,000 ha, it said.
The combined peas and beans crop was seen rising by 200,000 tonnes over 1996 to 4.3 million tonnes.
